precepts.text: Behold, I will make my words in thy mouth fire, and this people wood, and it shall devour them. That's some good stuff right there.
precepts.point: Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan: our comings is supposed to be after Christ the Lord, but the white man's comings and goings is after Satan. That goes back to Genesis 4.
precepts.why:
Paul says the Wicked shall be revealed, “whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth.” The spirit of God's mouth is the holy Bible, and Jeremiah 5:14 shows how it consumes: “behold, I will make my words in thy mouth fire, and this people wood, and it shall devour them.”

Some of us speak very well and have eloquent words, and that is fine, but we must use God's word; that is where the power is. We read the Bible but don't see the spiritual effect it has in this realm, because our eyes are closed. God is saying, my word is fire. Speak it whether they hear or forbear. Even those who reject it are at home tossing and tumbling in their beds, because the way it is broken down haunts them.

As we teach the word of God, we are judging, and many are being marked for death. Everyone who hears it and rejects it and refuses it: remember that Christ said it will be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah than for those who do not hear his messengers. The words are the fire, the people who reject them are the wood, and that is how the Lord consumes the wicked with the spirit of his mouth.

precepts.text: Like as ye have forsaken me, and served strange gods in your land, so shall ye serve strangers in a land that is not yours. We are serving strangers in a land that is not ours.
precepts.point: They are the most needy of any people in our country, the book said. It does say needy, and the Bible says it too.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
The masters' own book says of us: they are in the eye of the law property. In the eyes of their laws, we were their property. The Lord told us why: “And it shall come to pass, when ye shall say, Wherefore doeth the Lord our God all these things unto us? then shalt thou answer them, Like as ye have forsaken me, and served strange gods in your land, so shall ye serve strangers in a land that is not yours.”

We are serving strangers in a land that is not ours, a land we are not familiar with. That is the servitude the Lord allowed because we forsook him.

So the slavery here was the curse on Israel for serving strange gods, not the obedience Colossians 3:22 teaches between Israelite servants and Israelite masters. They took the scripture and used it to hold us as property, but the Lord had already told us we would serve strangers.

precepts.text: The prophets prophesy falsely, and the priests bear rule by their means, and my people love to have it so. You love to have it so, but you are not valiant for God's laws, and you will suffer the consequences because you had a space to repent and rejected it for a fool. Tell them the truth and they say not my Jesus; call him a stripper and they say amen.
precepts.point: Because judgment is not executed speedily they think they can say anything about Jesus; he is writing it in a book and coming back to say, say that to my face. That is how you know Jesus is a black man.

note.label: Fixx Ya Face Fridays | as Was Supposed!!

precepts.why:
Watch this: they know they are up there speaking outside the Bible. He didn't have a Bible in his hand, just the silly glasses and the loud outfit. “The prophets prophesy falsely, and the priests bear rule by their means; and my people love to have it so”.

What baffles us about Christianity is that when you give them the truth out of the Bible, they say, not my Jesus. But when somebody said he was a stripper, nobody said not my Jesus. Everybody said amen. Tell them Christ is coming back to give us glory and set up his kingdom on earth and we're going to rule it, and it's not my Jesus. My people love to have it so.

You love to have it so, but you are not valiant for God's laws. So when Christ comes back, “with ten thousands of his saints, To execute judgment upon all”, you will suffer the consequences, because you had a space to repent and you rejected it for some fool saying Christ was a stripper instead of saying he is your Lord and Saviour. He is going to hold you accountable for what you did or did not do while you had the opportunity. This is the King of kings and Lord of lords, and you lowered him to a woman selling her body in a strip club.

precepts.text: Seek in the streets for a man that executes judgment and seeks truth; He struck them but they refused correction and to return.
precepts.point: Day and night they go about seeking violence; wickedness is in the midst and deceit and guile depart not from her streets.

note.label: Psalm 55: Cast Thy Burden Upon the Lord

precepts.why:
“Run ye to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem, and see now, and know, and seek in the broad places thereof, if ye can find a man, if there be any that executeth judgment, that seeketh the truth; and I will pardon it.” Seek in the streets for a man that executes judgment and seeks truth. In David's city, deceit and guile depart not from her streets, and it is the same in ours.

“O Lord, are not thine eyes upon the truth? thou hast stricken them, but they have not grieved; thou hast consumed them, but they have refused to receive correction: they have made their faces harder than a rock; they have refused to return.” He struck them, but they have not grieved; they refused correction and refused to return. That is why the violence and strife stay in the city: we are cursed in it and have not turned.

precepts.text: Because of these words, the Lord makes His words in the mouth fire and this people wood, and it shall devour them; God's word and His law are like fire.
precepts.point: He shall drink of the brook in the way, therefore shall He lift up the head. God is waiting on us, on Israel, to keep His laws so He can activate and do His thing.

note.label: Psalm 110: Sit Thou at My Right Hand

precepts.why:
“Wherefore thus saith the Lord God of hosts, Because ye speak this word, behold, I will make my words in thy mouth fire, and this people wood, and it shall devour them.” God's word and his law are like fire, and the people are wood.

That is why the destroying of the heathen is without labour: the law that is like fire devours them. He fills the places with the dead bodies and wounds the heads over many countries by his word in the mouth.

precepts.text: Everyone that heareth His sayings and doeth them not is likened to a foolish man who built his house upon the sand, and great was the fall of it.
precepts.point: Even the great men who should have known the way have altogether broken the yoke and burst the bonds.
precepts.why:
“And every one that heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, which built his house upon the sand”, and great was the fall of it. That is what foolish means here. The poor are foolish; they “know not the way of the Lord, nor the judgment of their God”, for when you sin you should know a judgment comes behind it. They hear and do not do, and their house is built on sand.

And it is not only the poor. Even the great men, who “have known the way of the Lord, and the judgment of their God”, who should have known the way, “have altogether broken the yoke, and burst the bonds.” Great was the fall of it.

precepts.text: The Most High foretold He would bring a nation from the end of the earth, swift as an eagle, of fierce countenance and strange tongue, that regards neither old nor young.
precepts.point: He will bring a mighty and ancient nation from far, whose language they know not, upon the house of Israel.
precepts.why:
“The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth; a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand; A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old, nor shew favour to the young”. The Most High foretold this long before Jeremiah: a nation from the end of the earth, swift as an eagle, of fierce countenance and strange tongue, that regards neither old nor young.

Jeremiah says the same thing to the house of Israel: “it is a mighty nation, it is an ancient nation, a nation whose language thou knowest not, neither understandest what they say.” Because they spoke against him, the Most High made his words in Jeremiah's mouth fire and this people wood, to devour them, and everything Jeremiah said came to pass.

precepts.text: That same mighty and ancient nation, whose language we knew not, would eat up our harvest, bread, flocks, and herds, and it came to pass with the Chaldeans.
precepts.point: This should sound familiar; the same siege and famine came on us again under the Romans in 70 A.D. These are generational curses that fall on multiple generations when we break the Most High's commandments.

note.label: Jeremiah 52: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Puppet King Zedekiah

precepts.why:
Jeremiah himself had told them: “Lo, I will bring a nation upon you from far, O house of Israel, saith the Lord: it is a mighty nation, it is an ancient nation, a nation whose language thou knowest not, neither understandest what they say.” “Their quiver is as an open sepulchre, they are all mighty men.”

That same nation would “eat up thine harvest, and thy bread, which thy sons and thy daughters should eat: they shall eat up thy flocks and thine herds: they shall eat up thy vines and thy fig trees: they shall impoverish thy fenced cities, wherein thou trustedst, with the sword.” It came to pass with the Chaldeans: Nebuchadnezzar and all his army pitched against Jerusalem and built forts round about, and by the fourth month the famine was so sore in the city that there was no bread for the people of the land.

Yet “in those days, saith the Lord, I will not make a full end with you.” And when they ask “Wherefore doeth the Lord our God all these things unto us?” the answer is given: “Like as ye have forsaken me, and served strange gods in your land, so shall ye serve strangers in a land that is not yours.” These are the generational curses that fall on multiple generations when we break the Most High's commandments, and the same siege and famine came on us again under the Romans in 70 A.D.

precepts.text: Behold, I will make my words in thy mouth fire; when the tongues appeared like fire, they spoke the word of the Most High in the scattered nations' languages.
precepts.point: Because Israel was scattered among nations whose tongue they did not understand, the Most High spoke to his people with stammering lips and another tongue. The cloven tongues were the many languages of the lands where Israel was dispersed, and they spoke the word of the Most High in them like fire.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
The tongues appeared “like as of fire”, and Jeremiah shows what the fire is: “Because ye speak this word, behold, I will make my words in thy mouth fire, and this people wood, and it shall devour them.” The word of the Most High in a man's mouth is fire.

That is what came upon the apostles. The divided tongues were the many languages of the lands where Israel was scattered, and in those languages they spoke the word of the Most High like fire.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: God’s words have the power, not our own words. “Behold, I will make my words in thy mouth fire, and this people wood, and it shall devour them”: this whole thing is spiritual. God’s words burn them up on the inside, so use his words.

points: Run through the streets of Jerusalem and seek in the broad places for a man that executeth judgment and seeketh the truth, and if one righteous man be found the Most High will pardon it.
Though they say the Lord liveth, they swear falsely; He has stricken and consumed them, but they refused correction and made their faces harder than a rock.
The poor are foolish and know not the way of the Most High nor the judgment of their God, for when you sin you should know a judgment comes behind it.
Even the great men who should have known the way have altogether broken the yoke and burst the bonds.
A lion out of the forest, a wolf of the evenings, and a leopard shall watch over their cities and tear in pieces everyone that goes out, because their transgressions are many.
This judgment comes through the Most High using the other nations against His people.
How shall He pardon them, when their children have forsaken Him and sworn by them that are no gods, bowing down and swearing to idols.

When He had fed them to the full they committed adultery and assembled in the harlot's house, every one neighing after his neighbor's wife; shall He not visit for these things and be avenged on such a nation.
Go up upon her walls and destroy, but make not a full end, and take away her battlements, for they are not the Most High's at this time.
The house of Israel and the house of Judah have dealt very treacherously against Him, as our people still do today.
They belied the Most High and said it is not He, neither shall evil, sword, nor famine come upon them, denying that judgment would fall.
The prophets shall become wind and the word is not in them, for there was no teaching going on.
Because Jeremiah speaks this word, the Most High will make His words in his mouth fire to devour the people, and everything Jeremiah said came to pass.
He will bring a mighty and ancient nation from far, whose language they know not, upon the house of Israel.
Their quiver is as an open sepulchre and they are all mighty men, the best of the nation for war against us.
They shall eat up the harvest, the bread, the flocks, the herds, the vines, and the figs, and impoverish the fenced cities that Israel trusted in with the sword.
Even in those days He will not make a full end, but will leave a remnant when He brings the judgment.

Because they forsook Him and served strange gods in their land, they shall serve strangers in a land that is not theirs, which is exactly our condition today, working and giving it right back to our oppressors.
Declare to the foolish people without understanding, who have eyes and see not and ears and hear not, asking whether they will not fear Him.
He placed the sand for the bound of the sea by a perpetual decree, a law the waters cannot pass though they toss and roar, yet the people still do not fear that power.
These people have a revolting and rebellious heart and will not say in their heart, let us fear the Most High who gives the former and latter rain in his season.
Their iniquities have turned away these things, for the Most High wants to bless us, but we cannot be blessed while in the midst of sin.
Among His people are found wicked men who lay wait as one that sets snares, catching men as a cage full of birds, which is happening today as we rob and kill one another.
Their houses are full of deceit; they are waxen fat and shining and overpass the deeds of the wicked, yet they judge not the cause of the fatherless nor the right of the needy.
Shall He not visit for these things and be avenged on such a wicked nation.

A wonderful and horrible thing is committed in the land: the prophets prophesy falsely, the priests bear rule by their means, and the people love to have it so; what will they do in the end when it is time to be judged.
